title: Travel reaches record levels in a resilient outlook
gist: Oxford Economics promotes a 3 November webinar saying global travel arrivals are on course for a record year despite Middle East conflict, Asian diplomatic rifts and North American tariff tensions, with a strong rebound expected in 2027.

insights.claim: Conflict in the Middle East, diplomatic rifts across Asia and tariff tensions in North America have slowed global travel, yet arrivals are still on course for a record year.
insights.so_what: Travel demand is resilient to geopolitical drag, supporting travel-linked equities.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects a strong travel rebound in 2027, while flagging risks that could get in the way.
insights.so_what: A 2027 rebound call is a constructive signal for airlines and lodging, though the piece is a webinar promotion without figures.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
